title: Coral and the Ledger
premise: In 1918, on a storm-battered coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Jude Villalobos has spent the war perfecting invisibility, tending his light and his late wife's unfinished workshop of tide-driven automata. When a mute child named Coral is abandoned at his door with a note instructing him to forget her face, he recognizes her as the daughter of a smuggled deserter whose ledger of bribed officials is hidden inside one of the workshop machines. As storms and a corrupt naval officer close in, Jude must complete the machine that will expose the ledger before the armistice renders the crime unpunishable; in the end he chooses justice over safety, loses the workshop to fire, but saves Coral, the ledger's truth, and his own capacity to love again.
about_author: S. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs from the First World War era. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of history.

chapters.title: The Light That Keeps Nothing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes his routine, grief for his wife Elena, and the half-finished workshop of her tide-powered automata. He believes history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: numb endurance, the comfort of small repeated tasks.

chapters.title: A Knock Between Storms
chapters.summary: During a gale, Jude finds a child asleep on his doorstep with a note: 'Forget this face.' Coral won't speak. He intends to hand her to authorities at first light. Beat: reluctant compassion cracking open routine.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, fragmentary. She watches Jude, tests his kindness, hides a brass key on a cord around her neck. Flashback shards of a boat, a man's voice, running. Beat: fear learning to trust.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Counts Waves
chapters.summary: Naval Lieutenant Harrow visits, ostensibly inspecting the light, really asking questions about boats and faces. Jude lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Beat: dread — invisibility is already compromised.

chapters.title: Elena's Machines
chapters.summary: Jude shows Coral the workshop to occupy her; she gravitates to a locked cabinet automaton she seems to recognize. He discovers Elena left blueprints unfinished. Beat: wonder reawakening grief into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Bird
chapters.summary: Coral finally speaks one word: 'Papa.' Following her gestures, Jude finds a hollow songbird automaton containing a coded ledger of bribes paid to officials smuggling deserters — including Harrow's name. Beat: revelation; history arrives at his door.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Coral's father Mateo's POV in letters Jude decodes: he hid the ledger, sent his daughter to the one man who owed him silence — a debt from Jude's own past. Beat: guilt; Jude was never uninvolved.

chapters.title: The Debt of Salt
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He recalls how Mateo once saved him from drowning and asked nothing. Now the debt is called due. He decides not to report Coral. Beat: choice made; duty inverted.

chapters.title: Harrow Returns
chapters.summary: Harrow searches the station under pretext of contraband inspection. Jude hides Coral in the lamp room among rotating lenses. Harrow notices the workshop lock is scratched. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension.

chapters.title: Learning to Speak Again
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude. Coral teaches herself Elena's tools; Jude teaches her stars. She speaks in full sentences for the first time: 'Are you going to forget my face?' He says no. Beat: found family forming.

chapters.title: The Armistice Rumor
chapters.summary: News arrives that peace talks may conclude within weeks; after armistice, wartime courts dissolve and the ledger's crimes become untouchable. A deadline crystallizes: finish the decoding machine before the guns stop. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone burns Elena's blueprint chest. Jude suspects the visiting supply boatman; Coral saw a man with a naval coat. Beat: violation and fury; the enemy is inside their small world.

chapters.title: The Boatman's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude confronts the boatman, who admits Harrow paid him but pleads he has children too. Jude lets him go with a warning. Beat: moral complexity — everyone is surviving at a price.

chapters.title: Rebuilding From Memory
chapters.summary: Jude and Coral reconstruct the decoder from memory and Coral's recollection of her father's descriptions. Working nights by lamplight, they grow closer. Beat: hope through collaboration; love against duty taking shape.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Harrow offers Jude a promotion and mainland transfer if he surrenders 'the item.' Jude refuses, understanding he's choosing ruin. That night he almost sends Coral away to protect her. Beat: temptation and sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Great Storm Warning
chapters.summary: The year's worst storm approaches just as the final component must be cast. Harrow schedules his raid for the same night, betting weather will isolate the station. Beat: converging threats; no way out but through.

chapters.title: Night of the Rising Water
chapters.summary: Storm hits. The light must be kept burning or ships die — but keeping it means Jude can't guard the workshop. He splits himself between two duties. Beat: impossible arithmetic of responsibility.

chapters.title: Fire in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Harrow's men torch the workshop during the storm's peak. Coral runs in to save the bird automaton; Jude follows into the flames. They escape with the ledger as the roof collapses. Beat: climax begins; everything material is lost.

chapters.title: The Light Against the Dark
chapters.summary: Harrow corners them at the lamp room; in the struggle the great lens cracks and the beam falters. Jude uses Elena's largest automaton — the tide-engine — to trap Harrow until the supply cutter arrives with witnesses. Beat: physical and moral climax; justice seized outside the law.

chapters.title: Armistice Morning
chapters.summary: Bells ring; the war ends. Harrow is arrested as the ledger is read aloud by an arriving magistrate. The crimes are entered into record hours before amnesty could have buried them. Beat: catharsis; history happened here, to them.

chapters.title: Ashes and Seeds
chapters.summary: Jude surveys the burned workshop and decides not to rebuild it exactly — instead a schoolroom and garden. Coral asks if she can stay. He says the light needs two keepers now. Beat: tender resolution; grief transmuted.

chapters.title: Coral and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Coral's POV years later. She keeps the light beside Jude, the restored songbird on the mantel singing its coded tune only they understand. Some histories are kept alive deliberately. Beat: continuity, chosen family, memory as inheritance.
